subject.title: [Feature]: Optimization for Dockerfile.sandbox-common # add retries and fix-missings for apt-get

question: Should the sandbox Dockerfile fix be retry-only, or should OpenClaw intentionally accept `--fix-missing` partial-install semantics for these sandbox images?
rationale: `Acquire::Retries` addresses the transient-network goal, while `--fix-missing` changes package-install failure behavior and may produce incomplete sandbox images unless maintainers explicitly want that contract.

options.title: Use retry-only APT installs
options.body: Keep `Acquire::Retries` for network fetch resilience but remove `--fix-missing` so required sandbox packages still fail closed after retries.

options.title: Accept partial-install behavior
options.body: Keep `--fix-missing` only if maintainers intentionally want builds to proceed after missing packages and add package-presence verification or documentation for that contract.

options.title: Replace the linked PR
options.body: If the current branch is not revised and proven, close or supersede it with a narrower retry-only PR.

recommendation.title: Use retry-only APT installs
recommendation.body: Keep `Acquire::Retries` for network fetch resilience but remove `--fix-missing` so required sandbox packages still fail closed after retries.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent commits show ownership of the sandbox common Dockerfile, setup script, and smoke workflow that would validate this decision.
